chunks.text: The expected operating life of the washable parts is one to three months. Check whether the product operates normally before use. Use beyond service life may reduce performance; incorrect vacuum control or excessive vacuum may cause injury.

Keep the pump motor dry. The diaphragm must be completely dry. Attach the diaphragm silicone to the milk cup lid before assembly to prevent air leakage. Detach the milk collector from the pump motor before pouring. Assemble the valve and milk collector correctly. Attach the flange and pump motor tightly so there is no air leakage or loss of suction.

Parts include the flange cover, 24 mm flange, pump motor, milk collector, diaphragm, valve, milk collector lid, and magnetic charging cable. Assemble only clean, dry parts and make sure every seal is seated correctly.

A properly fitted flange maximizes milk output, helps prevent nipple damage, and supports effective pumping. Measure the nipple and select the matching insert: the guide shows 15 mm inserts for about 11-13 mm nipples, 17-21 mm inserts for about 13-20 mm nipples, and the 24 mm flange without an insert for about 20-23 mm nipples. Recheck comfort and fit during pumping.

Center the nipple in the flange tunnel and press the flange to the breast with no gap. Secure the pump in the bra so it stays firmly against the breast. Correct nipple alignment is important for comfort and performance.

Controls include Mode Selection, Decrease Suction Level, Increase Suction Level, and On/Off or Pause/Continue. Long-press the power button to turn the pump on or off; short-press it to pause or continue. Battery full is solid white; low battery with one cycle left is solid red; charging flashes green; fully charged is solid green.

Press and hold the on/off button for 2 seconds until the indicator light turns white and flashes. Separate the pump motor from the milk collector. With the bottle lid facing upward, open the silicone seal on the pouring spout and pour out the milk.

Detach the flange from the pump, remove the diaphragm, disassemble the milk collector, and separate the valve. The pump motor and charging parts are non-washable. Wash milk-contact parts, keep parts away from the heated container edges, and dry accessories thoroughly before reassembly. Do not put parts directly into a microwave; use a suitable microwave steam sterilizer bag according to its instructions.

Use a USB Type-C charging cable to charge the charging case. The four charging-case lights indicate approximately 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% battery from left to right. Short-press the charging-case control to show or hide the battery indicator.
The product is recommended for use with the Momcozy app. Download the app from an official app store. For product questions, the quick guide lists support@momcozy.com.

7.5.Storing breastmilk 7.5.1.Proper Storage of Breast Milk Following therecommended storage andpreparation techniques can maintain the safety and quality of expressed breast milk for the baby's health. These are general guidelines for storing human milk at different temperatures. Various factors affect how long human milk can be stored safely.Suchfactors include milk volume,room temperature when milkis expressed,temperature fluctuations in the refrigerator and freezer, and cleanliness of the environment. Storingbreastmilk after expressing: ·Refrigerate or chill milk right after it is pumped, if possible.You can put it in the refrigerator,place it in a cooler or insulated cooler pack, or freeze it in small (2 to 4 ounce)batchesfor later feedings. ·Use breast milk storage bags or clean,food-grade containers to store expressed breast milk. Make sure the containers are made of glass or plastic and have tight-fitting lids. --Avoid bottles with the recycle symbol number 7,which indicates that the container maybemadeofBPA-containingplastic. ·Remove air before sealing. ·Lay bags flat to freeze. To prevent sticking between bags, please separate the bags with paper towels. ·Never store breast milk in disposable bottle liners or plastic bags that are not intended for storingbreast milk. ·Gently swirl the container to mix the cream part of the breast milk that may rise to the top back into the rest of the milk.Do not shake the milk.
